MAX_NESTING_DEPTH

Security hardening (GHSA braces <=3.0.3): both parse and expand walk brace nodes recursively, so a pattern like {{{{…}}}} nested thousands of levels deep exhausts the call stack before any range/limit check runs. Glob patterns in this dependency's consumers (micromatch, stylelint, fast-glob) never nest braces deeper than a handful of levels, so a small ceiling closes the hole without changing any legitimate behavior.

assertSafeNesting

Scans a pattern for unescaped {/} nesting depth and throws before the recursive parser/expander can be driven into stack exhaustion. Backslash escapes are honored so \{ does not count toward the depth.

  • @param {String} input Brace pattern to validate.
  • @param {Number} [depth] Recursion accumulator for the character loop.

braces

Expand the given pattern or create a regex-compatible string.

const braces = require('braces');
console.log(braces('{a,b,c}', { compile: true })); //=> ['(a|b|c)']
console.log(braces('{a,b,c}')); //=> ['a', 'b', 'c']
  • @param {String} str
  • @param {Object} options

(module scope)

Parse the given str with the given options.

// braces.parse(pattern, [, options]);
const ast = braces.parse('a/{b,c}/d');
console.log(ast);
  • @param {String} pattern Brace pattern to parse
  • @param {Object} options

(module scope)

Creates a braces string from an AST, or an AST node.

const braces = require('braces');
let ast = braces.parse('foo/{a,b}/bar');
console.log(stringify(ast.nodes[2])); //=> '{a,b}'
  • @param {String} input Brace pattern or AST.
  • @param {Object} options

(module scope)

Compiles a brace pattern into a regex-compatible, optimized string. This method is called by the main braces function by default.

const braces = require('braces');
console.log(braces.compile('a/{b,c}/d'));
//=> ['a/(b|c)/d']
  • @param {String} input Brace pattern or AST.
  • @param {Object} options

(module scope)

Expands a brace pattern into an array. This method is called by the main braces function when options.expand is true. Before using this method it's recommended that you read the performance notes) and advantages of using .compile instead.

const braces = require('braces');
console.log(braces.expand('a/{b,c}/d'));
//=> ['a/b/d', 'a/c/d'];
  • @param {String} pattern Brace pattern
  • @param {Object} options

(module scope)

Processes a brace pattern and returns either an expanded array (if options.expand is true), a highly optimized regex-compatible string. This method is called by the main braces function.

const braces = require('braces');
console.log(braces.create('user-{200..300}/project-{a,b,c}-{1..10}'))
//=> 'user-(20[0-9]|2[1-9][0-9]|300)/project-(a|b|c)-([1-9]|10)'
  • @param {String} pattern Brace pattern
  • @param {Object} options
